facts.name: Online MSE purpose
facts.detail: The about page describes the online M.S. in Software Engineering as preparation for careers as software engineers and software project managers.
facts.quote: The Master of Science in Software Engineering (MSE) is an online program that prepares individuals for careers as software engineers and software project managers in industry and government agencies.

facts.name: Process-oriented curriculum
facts.detail: The curriculum is described as a process-oriented approach grounded in software engineering research, theory, principles, and practice, including CMMI, ISO, agile, Scrum, XP, and architecture/design patterns.
facts.quote: The program emphasizes a comprehensive and thorough process-oriented approach to software development, and its curriculum is fundamentally grounded in software engineering research, theory, principles, and practice

facts.name: Designed for working professionals
facts.detail: The program is designed for professionals working in computer science who want graduate education in software engineering.
facts.quote: The program is designed for professionals working in the field of computer science who wish to further their skills and pursue graduate level education in Software Engineering.

facts.name: Culminating practicum project
facts.detail: The culminating activity is a practicum project on a large-scale software project, not a thesis.
facts.quote: The culminating activity of the M.S. will be a practicum project where each student applies his or her knowledge and skills to a large-scale software project.

facts.name: 100% online asynchronous
facts.detail: The home page states that all courses are 100% online with asynchronous delivery.
facts.quote: All courses 100% online

facts.name: No I-20 for this program
facts.detail: The FAQ says an I-20 cannot be issued because the program is offered entirely online.
facts.quote: An I-20 cannot be issued for the MSE program, since it is offered entirely online. U.S. immigration policy prohibits the student visa for entirely online programs.

facts.name: Distinct from on-campus AMSE
facts.detail: CSUF also offers an on-campus Accelerated M.S. in Software Engineering (AMSE), operated by Extension and International Programs; the online MSE is operated by the Computer Science department.
facts.quote: CSUF offers two software engineering programs: the online MSE program and the on-campus Accelerated Master of Science in Software Engineering (AMSE) program.

facts.name: Degree title has no 'Online'
facts.detail: The FAQ says the word Online will not appear on the diploma; the degree is Master of Science in Software Engineering.
facts.quote: No. Although this is a fully online program, the degree itself is a "Master of Science in Software Engineering." The word "Online" will not appear on your degree.

facts.name: Program length
facts.detail: The FAQ says the online MSE regularly takes 22 months; AMSE takes 17 months.
facts.quote: Regularly MSE takes 22 months, while AMSE takes 17 months to complete.

facts.name: University GPA
facts.detail: Applicants need an acceptable baccalaureate degree with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.5 for Computer Science undergraduates or 3.0 for other degree holders.
facts.quote: The applicant must have completed four-year college course of study and hold an acceptable baccalaureate degree with a minimum/cumulative grade point average of 2.5 for applicants having an undergraduate degree in Computer Science or 3.0 for other degree holders.

facts.name: Transcripts
facts.detail: An official transcript is required from each university or college attended.
facts.quote: An official transcript is required from each university or college you have attended.

facts.name: International English scores
facts.detail: International students must meet a minimum of 550 paper or 80 TOEFL, 6.5 Academic IELTS, or 58 PTE.
facts.quote: For international students: a minimum score of 550 (paper) or 80 in TOEFL or 6.5 Academic in IELTS or 58 in PTE.

facts.name: Software engineering background
facts.detail: Applicants should have taken an introductory software engineering course equivalent to CPSC 362 or have work experience in software development.
facts.quote: The applicant should have taken an Introductory Software Engineering course (equivalent with CPSC 362 at CSUF) or should have work experience in software development.

facts.name: Work-experience alternative
facts.detail: The FAQ says at least one year of software development experience is expected if the applicant has not completed CPSC 362 or an equivalent course, and a resume should be emailed to the program.
facts.quote: To apply, at least one year of experience in software development is expected.

facts.name: GRE not required
facts.detail: The FAQ says the GRE is not required.
facts.quote: No, we do not require the GRE.

facts.name: TOEFL/IELTS when needed
facts.detail: TOEFL/IELTS is needed if the applicant has not earned at least 72 college-level units in the U.S. or another majority English-speaking country.
facts.quote: Yes, if you have not earned at least 72 college-level units in the U.S. or another majority English-speaking country. Residency/citizenship is irrelevant to this requirement.

facts.name: No exit exam or thesis
facts.detail: There is no exit exam; students complete a terminal project in CPSC 597, and there is no thesis option.
facts.quote: No, there is no exit exam. Students are required to complete a significant terminal project as part of the curriculum (CPSC 597). There is no thesis option.

facts.name: One course per semester costs the same
facts.detail: Students may take only one course per semester, but it costs the same as taking two, and each course is offered once per year.
facts.quote: Yes, but this will cost the same as taking two courses per semester. Also, since MSE offers each course once per year, you will need to wait a year if you miss taking a certain course.
facts.holdReason: Hold: Fullerton MSE cost fact (Fall 2023 rates / cost wording). Awaiting Achsah refresh decision.

facts.name: No program-level scholarship
facts.detail: The FAQ says there is no scholarship at the program level and points to university financial aid.
facts.quote: There is no scholarship at the program level. However, you may check the university Financial Aid website for available funding opportunities.
